_note: Quiz bank. 'answer' is a 0-based index into options; 'img' is an optional picture.

questions.q: An attacker's feet are exactly LEVEL with the second-last defender when the pass is played. What is the decision?
options: Offside, but only if he scores
questions.why: Level counts as onside. He must be nearer the goal line than the second-last opponent to be in an offside position.

questions.q: An attacker's body is behind the defender, but his outstretched arm is ahead of the defender. Offside?
options: Yes — any part of the body counts
Yes, if the arm touches the ball
No — arms and hands are not used to judge offside
questions.why: Only the head, body and feet count. Hands and arms are ignored.

questions.q: A throw-in is taken. The receiver is far beyond the last defender. What happens?
options: Play on — there is no offside from a throw-in
Offside only if he is past the keeper
questions.why: You can't be offside directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner.

questions.q: An attacker is in an offside position, but he does not touch the ball or affect any defender. The ball goes out of play. Offence?
options: Yes, but only inside the penalty area
Yes, if he was nearer than 5 metres to a defender
No — being in an offside position is not an offence by itself
Yes — the position is the offence
questions.why: The offence is being INVOLVED in active play, not just standing there.

questions.q: Which is the correct description of a 3-5-2?
questions.why: Formations are written from defence to attack, not counting the goalkeeper.

questions.q: A 3-5-2 team loses the ball. The wing-backs drop deep. What shape does it often become?
questions.why: Wing-backs join the three centre-backs, so it becomes a back five.

questions.q: A 'false nine' drops into midfield. What problem does that cause the centre-backs?
options: Nothing — the false nine can't touch the ball
They must swap positions with the goalkeeper
Follow him and leave a hole, or let him go and give him time
questions.why: A false nine pulls defenders out of position or gets free time.

questions.q: Look at the picture in this step. A compact, narrow team is most likely to be beaten:
questions.why: Narrow = strong in the middle but gives space wide.

questions.q: Team A has a PPDA of 6. Team B has a PPDA of 14. Which team presses harder?
options: Team B — a bigger number means more pressing
Team A — the opponents get fewer passes before an action
You can't tell without the xG
questions.why: PPDA = passes allowed per defensive action. Lower = more intense press.

questions.q: Which is the BEST example of a pressing trigger?
options: The opponent takes a throw-in near his own goal
The opponent has a clear shot at goal
The referee starts the second half
The opponent passes backwards to his goalkeeper
questions.why: A backward pass gives the receiver limited options — a good moment to close in.

questions.q: What is the main risk of a high press?
options: Your goalkeeper must leave the pitch
One long pass beats the press and leaves space behind your defence
The referee gives more yellow cards
You can never win a corner
questions.why: The more players push up, the more space you leave behind.

questions.q: What does 'counter-press' mean?
options: Defending only with 10 players behind the ball
Trying to win the ball back immediately after losing it
questions.why: The other team is disorganised right after winning the ball — the best moment to win it back.

questions.q: A team has a penalty (xG 0.76) plus shots of 0.05 and 0.12. What is its total xG?
A team loses 0-1 but had 2.4 xG against 0.4 xG. What is the best explanation?
options: The xG must have included the other team's goals
One game is noisy — they probably were unlucky or the keeper was great
They must be a bad team
questions.why: Over one match luck is large. Over a season xG predicts results better than goals.

questions.q: A team has 70% possession but only 0.3 xG. What does this show?
options: They had the ball a lot but made very few good chances
questions.why: Possession is not the same as chance quality.

questions.q: A striker scores more than his xG for five seasons in a row. The most sensible conclusion is that he is:
questions.why: One season could be luck — five seasons suggests real finishing skill.

questions.q: What was Korea's best finish at the 2002 World Cup?
questions.why: Co-hosts Korea beat Italy and Spain, then lost to Germany in the semi-final.

questions.q: Which team did Korea beat 2-0 in the 2018 World Cup group stage?
questions.why: Germany went out in the group stage.

questions.q: Which club did Park Ji-sung play for from 2005 to 2012?
questions.why: Park spent seven years at Manchester United.

questions.q: In 2018, Korea's second goal against Germany went into an empty net. Why was it empty?
options: Korea scored from the halfway line with no goalkeeper
Germany had pushed everyone forward, even the goalkeeper, chasing a goal
questions.why: All-out attack means massive space at the other end.

questions.q: Look at the pass. Which ringed attacker is OFFSIDE when the ball is played?
questions.why: The orange-ringed attacker is beyond the yellow line (the second-last defender) and ahead of the ball. The white-ringed attacker is behind the line — onside.

questions.q: Look at the three shots. Which has the HIGHEST xG?
options: The silver ball — edge of the box
The gold ball — close to goal, central
They all have the same xG
questions.why: Distance and angle: close and central is by far the best chance.
questions.alt: Penalty area with a gold shot close in the middle, a silver shot on the edge of the box, an orange shot from a tight angle

questions.q: The gold, silver and orange shots have xG of 0.45, 0.07 and 0.03. What is the total?
questions.why: 0.45 + 0.07 + 0.03 = 0.55. Roughly half a goal.

questions.q: This formation is a 3-5-2. When the team defends, what will it most often look like?
options: A back three with five forwards
questions.why: The wing-backs drop back to join the three centre-backs.
questions.alt: Red dots: 1 goalkeeper, 3 defenders, 5 midfielders, 2 strikers

questions.q: In the same picture, what is the special job of the two widest midfielders?
options: They stay next to the goalkeeper
They are wing-backs: defend the whole flank and attack the whole flank
questions.why: A back three needs wing-backs to give width. They need huge stamina.

questions.q: Look at the press. Why are the red players standing in the passing lanes instead of just chasing the ball?
options: To trap the ball-carrier — no easy pass means an error
questions.why: A press works as a group: one presses the ball, the others cut the lanes.
questions.alt: Red players cutting off passing lanes around a blue defender with the ball

questions.q: A goal kick is taken. An attacker is far beyond the last defender and runs onto the ball. Decision?
options: Goal stands — no offside from a goal kick
Offside only if the keeper takes it
questions.why: Not offside directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner.

questions.q: A defender desperately blocks a shot and the ball bounces to an attacker who was in an offside position when the shot was taken. Decision?
options: Still offside — a block/deflection is not 'deliberate play'
No offence because there was a shot
questions.why: Only a deliberate play (like a controlled pass or clearance) resets offside. A block does not.

questions.q: Team A: 70% possession, 0.4 xG. Team B: 30% possession, 1.6 xG. Which statement is best supported?
options: Possession and xG measure the same thing
Team B created much better chances
questions.why: xG measures chance quality. B had the better chances with less of the ball.

questions.q: Team X: PPDA of 7.5. Team Y: PPDA of 16. Which statement is correct?
options: X presses more intensely and wins the ball higher up the pitch
questions.why: Lower PPDA = fewer passes allowed = more aggressive press.

questions.q: Korea beat Germany 2-0 in 2018, scoring after Germany pushed everyone forward. Which tactical idea does this show?
options: A high press from the first minute
A compact defence and counter-attack — punishing a team that overcommits
questions.why: Germany left huge spaces behind. A compact side that survives can hit them with the second ball.

questions.q: You lead 1-0 against a stronger team with 20 minutes left. Which plan fits best?
options: Compact mid/low block, win it back and counter-attack quickly
Take a risk by attacking with everyone
Press very high with a high line
Play 7-3-0 and give the ball away on purpose
questions.why: Protect the lead: stay compact, avoid the big spaces behind a high line, and hit on the counter when the ball is won.
